newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares end slightly lower in slack trade.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares end slightly lower in slack trade.

text.p: Latvian stocks traded sideways to slightly lower on Thursday amid sluggish activity.
Turnover was a paltry 39,000 lats, and the bourse index eased 0.32 percent to 382.96.
Three of the five officially-listed stocks eased. Only the Kaija fish factory gained, inching up to 2.17 lats from 2.15 lats in trade of 2,200 lats.
Unibanka held steady at 3.35 lats, turning over 8,400 lats.
Dealers said the market was still meandering after the four-day midsummer weekend.

In a longer-term trend, the market has also failed to pull out of a slump started in January after what analysts called a speculative rally. The market was now seen lacking big insitutional investors and largely insulated from trends elsewhere in the region and Europe.
The little money that is out there is mostly being channeled into privatisation vouchers ahead sales of key state enterprises, dealers said.
"The vouchers will suck in a lot of the money, away from the bourse, until at least September," said one dealer.
But some dealers noted the official list of stocks seemed to be stabilising despite the day's losses.
"The official list appears to have stabilised," said Andreta Petersone, a broker with Hansabank-Latvija.
"The Riga Transport Fleet (RTF) is down a bit, but its half-year results are expected to be good. So, it shouldn't fall much more," she said.
RTF shed 3.3 percent to 1.19 lats on Thursday in trade of 2,500 lats.
